name: hero
whatItDemonstrates: A document-editor-style toolbar that composes other Base UI components inside one Toolbar.Root: an alignment ToggleGroup whose buttons are rendered through Toolbar.Button, a Toolbar.Group of format buttons, a Select font picker whose trigger is rendered through Toolbar.Button, separators between the sections, and a trailing Toolbar.Link.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state in the demo; Select.Root keeps the font value internally (defaultValue="Helvetica") and ToggleGroup keeps the pressed alignment internally
nonTrivialInteractions: Toolbar.Button render={<Toggle />} composes toggles into the toolbar: the two alignment buttons live in one ToggleGroup (aria-label="Alignment") so pressing one releases the other, each identified to the group by value ("align-left"/"align-right") with an aria-label per button

Toolbar.Button render={<Select.Trigger />} composes a Select trigger into the toolbar: opening it shows a font popup (Helvetica/Arial) whose selected item is marked by Select.ItemIndicator, while Select.Value reflects the current font on the trigger and Select.Icon shows a caret

All controls participate in the Toolbar's default roving-focus arrow-key navigation spanning the two groups, the Select trigger, and the Toolbar.Link; Toolbar.Separator visually splits alignment / format / font / link sections and is skipped as a control
Pressed styling is data-attribute driven: data-pressed from the shared ToggleGroup state on the alignment buttons and [aria-pressed] on the toggles

Variant divergence (not styling): the css-modules variant passes alignItemWithTrigger={false} to Select.Positioner (`docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/toolbar/demos/hero/css-modules/index.tsx:47-51`), so the popup positions against the trigger anchor and gets a real data-side value, while the tailwind variant uses the default alignItemWithTrigger=true (`docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/toolbar/demos/hero/tailwind/index.tsx:44-55`), which aligns the selected item with the trigger and renders data-side="none" — leaving the css-modules popup's [data-side='none'] rule dead. Component parts, props, and interactions are otherwise identical between variants
